note: Reference cases for the decision functions each repository implements itself (CONTRACT section 12). Every expected value is written by hand from the contract text; none is the output of an implementation. Paths are abstract: they name no machine. 'role_separation' expects the sorted list of distinct codes. 'namespace' gives and expects path segments; a case with 'expect_error' expects a refusal with that code instead of a path. 'archive_tree' (revision 2) gives the corpus, holding and tree asked for, whether the target identity matched (T2), the manifest found in the tree root (or null), the files observed in the tree (re-read: path, size, sha256) and the manifest already there before the write (or null), and expects the sorted list of distinct codes; empty means complete. Its input digests are of the fixture bytes; its expected codes are written by hand. The other functions expect one state or one object.
